report:
The restricted assertions A–E are established under their stated hypotheses. I found no concrete mathematical defect in their proofs. The unchanged original S12 completion criterion is not established: there is no nonzero divisor realized at the global threshold, and no substantive proposed converse is stated and disproved with its antecedents satisfied. D is a valid smooth-data obstruction; E realizes a divisor strictly below the global threshold. Completing the missing inverse argument would require substantive new work.

A. Canonical subtraction covers the entire one-sided class. Off S=Supp(E), w=u−ell_E is bounded above and satisfies h_E+dd^c w≥0. The supplied epsilon-logarithm and truncation construction extends it across S. The exact background inequality survives because the smooth correction has zero coefficient-measure mass on S, whereas the Hessian restriction there is positive. Monotone local L1 convergence preserves this inequality. Patching distributions and taking their canonical representatives proves u=ell_E+w everywhere in the required sense. Conversely, every genuine h_E-psh w has finite supremum and yields a genuine u=ell_E+w. Bounded residual potentials correspond precisely to ordinary equivalence. For E=0 this reduces to the identity map.

The measure identity is valid. Outside S the relevant currents and smooth-background expansions agree. On S all non-pluripolar terms and smooth corrections have zero mass. Local truncation identities followed by monotone measure limits also justify this reasoning for the task’s possibly infinite top-degree measures; no global finiteness theorem is being applied. The task-granted maximal-subsolution characterization and attainment apply to the positive background h_E, proving B_leq=b_(h_E)(f) with attainment. This does not establish ordinary equivalence, stretching membership, finite mass, or positivity of the coefficient for arbitrary L1 data.

B. For every envelope competitor, w=v−ell_E satisfies integral w^+ dV≤integral(−ell_E)dV. Fixed coordinate corrections and submean inequalities therefore give a uniform bound on sup w. Consequently ell_E≤phi_E≤ell_E+K, including canonical values on S. The regularized-maximum calculation preserves the precise nonclosed background inequality; countable selection and monotone convergence produce a genuine envelope. Ordinary-equivalent potentials enter the exact stretching class through a_t=phi_E−tK_u. The reverse containment uses only its defining ordinary order. No envelope-equality characterization is substituted for stretching.

C. The primary equation results have the required hypotheses. For h or h_E, the source density is f dV divided by the corresponding background volume. Bounded data belong to Lp for p>1; smooth positive data give smooth real F. Kołodziej–Nguyen and Nguyen use i/π times partial-barpartial, requiring potentials multiplied by two. Tosatti–Weinkove uses i times partial-barpartial, requiring multiplication by 2π. Nguyen supplies uniqueness of the scalar, without requiring potential uniqueness at lambda=0. For bounded f, truncation is eventually stationary, hence b=c. A smooth residual solution gives ell_E+w in both prescribed classes, with the claimed exact finite equation and mass. Together with A and B this proves all three attained coefficients.

The strictness proof is correct without semipositivity or nefness of beta_E. Equality of the two scalars would make a=ell_E+w−v harmonic for the strictly elliptic operator defined by Q=sum eta^j wedge sigma^(n−1−j). Closure of Q is unnecessary. The supplied barrier proves the strong maximum conclusion. Since a tends to −infinity near S, its maximum occurs inside a complementary component. Constancy there contradicts approach to its nonempty boundary in S.

D. Scaling an initially dominated nonzero effective divisor preserves actual current domination and makes h−beta_E positive. Distributional subtraction then has a canonical h_E-psh representative, so the potential belongs to the whole one-sided class. A and strictness give the stated contradiction. Thus every smooth strictly positive density has a positive finite global threshold that admits no actual nonzero effective divisorial component.

E. The projective logarithm has the correct Poincaré–Lelong normalization. Only the horizontal degree m and vertical degree k term survives in the product expansion, giving CV0 and CV0(1−lambda)^k. The zero residual potential identifies the bounded scalars; lambda ell attains the restricted coefficients, its actual divisor component, finite equation, and stretching membership. Under the explicit additional assumption v_-(h0)=0, bounded factor pullbacks have masses approaching zero on both products. Positivity gives the reverse lower bound. If h0 were closed, Bedford–Taylor recursion makes the difference between its bounded Monge–Ampère product and h0^m globally dd^c-exact, so integration gives the fixed positive mass V0. This proves the conditional nonclosedness claim. No factor satisfying the antecedent has been constructed.

Supporting literature note, not a premise of these proofs: [Alehyane–Lu–Salouf, Theorem 5.7](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.02339) already establishes ordinary prescribed-type equations for nonzero Lp data, p>1, relative to their model potentials. Here phi_E satisfies their model conditions: equivalence gives P_h[phi_E]=phi_E, and ell_E is epsilon h-psh for epsilon sufficiently close to one because epsilon h−beta_E remains positive. This overlaps the existence portion of C. The three cited older equation results likewise already supply its smooth/bounded analytic ingredients. No novelty claim for A–E, or blanket literature claim that S12 remains open, is certified.

Harmless clarification: the neighborhoods used in the subtraction construction are local on relatively compact coordinate sets. No substantive repair of A–E is needed. The unindexed task passages below record granted background, which is excluded from the external-premise list.
